For You

You do not have to begin with everything at once.

Choose what is closest to what you are looking for. This page does not assume how you should feel.

I recently learned I am living with HIV

You remain your whole self.

A diagnosis is information about health, not a measure of a person’s worth, character, or future.

Next steps often include speaking with a health professional, understanding ART, and following a care plan. You do not have to master every term today.

Understand treatmentUnderstand U=U
Your privacy matters.

You can ask a provider how confidentiality, medical records, and access to your health information are handled.

I am considering an HIV test

Testing is a step toward knowing—not a reason to judge.

Appropriate timing can depend on the test and when a possible exposure occurred. A health professional can help determine whether testing or retesting is needed.

  • Ask which test is being used and what the result means.
  • Ask about the window period.
  • Understand how confidentiality is protected.
  • Ask what happens next, whatever the result.
Prototype note

Indonesian service listings are not included until addresses, hours, costs, and privacy practices can be verified.

My partner is living with HIV

Healthy relationships begin with information and respect.

Learn about ART and U=U, communicate without blame, and make health decisions with a qualified provider when needed.

Listen

Do not assume your partner wants to discuss their status at every moment.

Learn U=U

A maintained undetectable viral load means HIV is not sexually transmitted.

Respect privacy

Someone’s HIV status should not be shared without their consent.

My friend or family member is living with HIV

Support does not require perfect words.

“Thank you for trusting me. What kind of support would be helpful?”

Begin by listening. Avoid blaming questions, do not disclose someone else’s status, and correct myths when you hear them.
